Answer: B
Reason: The axial CT image (Figure 2b) demonstrates a calcified, stenotic lesion in the right pulmonary artery (indicated by the arrow), which is characteristic of chronic vascular obstruction seen in Takayasu arteritis rather than an acute thromboembolism. This chronic narrowing explains the patient's symptoms of dyspnea and chest pain in the setting of increased hemodynamic demand during pregnancy.
